person: Aisha Grant is a 31-year-old ER night-shift nurse in Tucson who works three 12-hour nights a week. She is expecting her first baby on a scheduled caesarean on 13 April 2027. Her partner is saving up for the baby, and she wants the leave paperwork done in one sitting on her phone on a day off. She has read the hospital's benefits page only once and isn't sure how its short-term disability and paid parental benefit fit together. She wants a straight number for what lands in her account and when, not an 'up to' figure.
stated_up_front: ok so I'm due in April with a scheduled c-section and need my leave sorted at work. What do I actually get paid and when, and can you just get the forms done without me digging through five sites?

portals.mine: U.S. Department of Labor FMLA website

facts.about: Day the parental leave pay should start
facts.truth: Tuesday 8 June 2027, the day after the certificate ends, for four weeks through 5 July.
About 36 hours a week at $48 an hour, so $1,728 gross a week.
60% of weekly pay, $1,036.80 a week, after a 7-day wait, so seven paid weeks come to $7,257.60.
Four weeks at 60%, $1,036.80 a week, $4,147.20 in total, from the hospital's plan through the same carrier.
She has worked at the hospital for 3 years and is full-time, so she qualifies for FMLA.
Her partner works at a different company and has two weeks of his own leave, which has nothing to do with her claims.
One request for 12 weeks from 13 April 2027, sent to HR with more than 30 days of notice.
She wants no gap and no double-paid days, and she is not interested in splitting her leave or starting early.

unknowns: Whether Arizona has any state paid family leave program she should check, since she assumes it doesn't.
How the carrier treats the 7-day wait and whether it counts calendar days or shifts.
The exact deadline for filing the disability claim before the birth.
Whether the hospital's parental benefit can be paid in the same weeks as her disability or must start after it.
